item.title: Oracle Launches AI Development Resources for RAG, Agents, and Database Integration
item.description:
Oracle Launches AI Development Resources for RAG, Agents, and Database Integration

Oracle has released a suite of technical resources to help developers build AI applications, agents, and systems using Oracle AI Database and OCI services. These materials include reference apps, notebooks, and workshops covering RAG, vector and hybrid search, AI agents, and agent memory, with practical examples using LangChain and LangGraph. The repository provides complete, working examples that showcase end-to-end implementations, including source code, deployment configurations, and documentation for understanding architectural patterns and best practices.

📚 Available Resources

  • Reference apps, notebooks, and workshops for RAG, vector and hybrid search, AI agents, and agent memory
  • Integration examples using LangChain and LangGraph
  • Applications demonstrating AI-powered solutions with Oracle technologies
  • Complete, working end-to-end implementations with source code and deployment configs

🧪 Featured Implementations

Application Description
Gamified fitness platform Built with Oracle 26ai JSON Duality Views (FastAPI + Redis), created live during a webinar
Intelligent RAG system Multi-agent Chain of Thought (CoT), PDF/Web/Repo processing, with Oracle AI Database 26ai integration
Financial services AI agent Uses Oracle AI Database as a unified memory core for vector, graph, spatial, and relational queries
Next.js chatbot Pairs Oracle AI Database 26ai SQL, vector, and hybrid search with typed generative UI components
Full-stack AI application Oracle JET UI, OCI Generative AI integration, Kubernetes deployment, and Terraform infrastructure
AI chat app Uses TanStack Start and Oracle 26ai Select AI to query a shoe store database with natural language
Team knowledge base Slack, GitHub and docs connectors; in-database ONNX embeddings; Oracle Text + vector hybrid retrieval with RRF through langchain-oracledb; per-caller access control via DBMS_RLS row policy; exposed to Claude Code over MCP and LangChain create_agent CLI
AI agent harness Migrates RAG corpus from MongoDB into Oracle AI Database 26ai while preserving vector search and enabling SQL/JSON Duality queries

🔧 Key Technologies

  • Oracle AI Database 26ai with JSON Duality Views
  • Vector and hybrid search capabilities
  • langchain-oracledb for integration
  • DBMS_RLS for row-level security and access control
  • ONNX embeddings processed in-database
  • Support for LangChain and LangGraph frameworks
  • OCI Generative AI service integration
  • Kubernetes and Terraform for deployment

item.title: Milvus Updates Python SDK Documentation and Development Workflow
item.description:
Milvus Updates Python SDK Documentation and Development Workflow

The Milvus Vector Database project has released documentation and guidelines for its Python SDK, outlining installation methods, contribution processes, and version management practices.

📦 Installation & Requirements

PyMilvus supports Python 3.9+ and can be installed via pip or pip3. Specific versions of PyMilvus can be installed or upgraded to the latest release using pip commands.

🛠️ Development Workflow

Local development for the project uses the uv package manager, which must be installed before running make targets. The process includes:

  • Running pre-commit hooks to automatically execute linting and formatting checks before each commit.
  • Retrieving protos matching generated files, with specific version details available in milvus-proto.

🔄 Testing & Versioning

Commits on the development branch are packaged and uploaded to Test PyPI. The package naming convention for development branches follows the format x.y.z.rc<dist>, where <dist> represents the number of commits differing from the most recent release. Installing these packages requires appending --extra-index-url to the pip command.

💬 Community & Documentation

Contributors are encouraged to read contribution guidelines before adding code. For discussions or problem-solving, the community can be reached in the Slack channel #py-milvus. Documentation for PyMilvus is available online at the project’s API reference URL.

#Milvus #PythonSDK #VectorDatabase #DevOps #Programming

Source: milvus-io/pymilvus

item.title: New Connector Enables Qdrant as a Storage Destination in Apache Spark
item.description:
New Connector Enables Qdrant as a Storage Destination in Apache Spark

A new connector has been released that enables Qdrant to serve as a storage destination in Apache Spark, a distributed computing framework designed for big data processing and analytics.

⚙️ Key features

The connector supports several options for handling and structuring data:

  • Vector Ingestion: The connector supports ingesting multiple named or unnamed, dense or sparse vectors.
  • Compatibility Options: The embedding_field and vector_name options are maintained for backward compatibility. It is recommended to use vector_fields and vector_names for named vectors.
  • Collection Requirements: Before loading data using the connector, a collection must be created in advance with the appropriate vector dimensions and configurations.

🚀 Setup and availability

To integrate the connector into a Spark environment, users must get the JAR file from one of the available sources:

  • Prepackaged JAR: The packaged jar file can be found on GitHub Releases or Maven Central.
  • Building from Source: Users can build the jar from source. This requires having JDK@8 and Maven installed. Running the build command in the project root writes the JAR file into the target directory by default.

#Qdrant #ApacheSpark #VectorDatabase #BigData #DataEngineering

Source: qdrant/qdrant-spark

item.title: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases Vector Store Backend Options
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases Vector Store Backend Options

Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases has updated its customer-managed configuration to support three distinct vector store backends for RAG use cases.

⚙️ Key details

Vector Store Backend Key Features and Capabilities
Amazon OpenSearch Service Provides high-speed results from in-memory data; supports k-NN and hybrid search (lexical and vector); available in managed cluster and serverless deployments.
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector Combines relational database capabilities with vector similarity search; supports IVFFlat and HNSW indexing, various distance metrics (L2, cosine, inner product), and vectors up to 2,000 dimensions.
Amazon S3 Vectors Native vector support within AWS cloud object storage; designed for cost-effective scaling with sub-second query performance.

💡 Why it matters

Different backends serve specific RAG requirements:

  • Ecommerce and Product Catalogs: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless is well suited for these use cases due to low millisecond query latency and hybrid search capabilities that combine semantic understanding with keyword matching. It also supports complex filtering and aggregations for faceted navigation (such as brand, color, or price).
  • Cost Efficiency: Amazon S3 Vectors can reduce vector storage costs by up to 90 percent compared to traditional vector databases.
  • Precision Tuning: Users can utilize multiple distance metrics, such as Euclidean distance or cosine similarity, to fine-tune product similarity calculations.

🚀 Availability

  • Amazon OpenSearch Serverless: Supports both Classic and NextGen collections.
  • Compatibility Note: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless NextGen collections (generally available May 2026) are not yet compatible with the Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases Retrieve API.

#AmazonBedrock #RAG #VectorDatabase #AWS

Source: Selecting a vector store for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases | Amazon Web Services
